TestDataDistribution::test_data_distribu.description: Starts a 3/4/6-node single-rack cluster, creates keyspace1 with RF=1 (128 initial tablets when tablets are enabled), writes 210k keys (21k in debug/coverage) with cassandra-stress using the parametrized compaction strategy (LCS/STCS/TWCS/ICS), then flushes and runs a major compaction. It asserts that each node's on-disk table size (du -h) and its nodetool status Load are within +-40% of the average, and that all nodes report the same size unit. This is a regression test for scylladb/scylladb#6193 (badly skewed random vnode tokens, so the seed node got much less data). With tablets it also checks end-to-end that the tablet allocator/balancer spreads data evenly.

origin.summary: Test data distribution between nodes; reproducer for scylladb/scylladb#6193 (fixed by scylla f3fd466156, dht get_random_token uint64).

TestDataDistribution::test_data_distribu.reason: Unique end-to-end check that real data ends up balanced on disk and in nodetool status Load (vnodes regression for #6193, plus tablets). Scylla tests only cover balancer logic/tablet counts (partial), and the pass rate is 99.8% over 972 runs. Note: slow (~126s x 12 params, ~25 min per build) and the compaction-strategy dimension adds little, since data placement doesn't depend on compaction strategy: trimming to one strategy x 3 node counts is worth considering. Note: @pytest.mark.single_node on a 3-6 node test is a mislabel (harmless, conftest.py:439 only changes the gossip-settle default). Note: the 'same unit' asserts (verify_datasize_*) fail spuriously if node sizes straddle a unit boundary (e.g. 1000M vs 1.1G) instead of normalizing.
